mathematical_checks: Two maximal constant runs of the same word and same symbol that overlap must have identical endpoints: otherwise one run's maximal boundary lies inside the other. This is a generic finite-word fact requiring no admissibility.

If a new maximal run contains an old physical c-position i, choose the old maximal run through i. descendant_step places i in its nonempty descendant, which is itself maximal in the whole new word; overlap uniqueness identifies it with the complete new run.

Two distinct old maximal runs cannot share that descendant: its nonempty interval lies inside both old intervals, forcing those old runs to overlap and coincide. Thus no merge/split counterexample is compatible with the existing theorem.

If no old physical c-position lies in the new run, every position satisfies L≤i or q i≠c, exactly the guarded BornRun predicate. Newly born bands may contain many sites, so uniqueness of a birth site is false.
Finite no-birth coverage needs existence of predecessors only; unique founder is a useful stronger interface but not necessary for4R+1 extinction.
For eventual absence, restart at the eventual no-birth time and use R=L_start, which bounds all its maximal runs. This avoids any uniform bound on run lengths over the entire orbit.
Birth timestamps index source transitions. A birth at transition s appears in state s+1; founder state time r equals s+1. Keep this offset explicit.
R=0 means no initial positive-length c-run and is permitted by the uniform4R+1 statement. No run or birth is assumed to exist by the hypotheses.
